back: Businesses that extract or grow natural resources: farming, fishing, forestry and mining.
Businesses that turn raw materials into goods: manufacturing, processing and construction.
Businesses that provide services: retail, transport, banking, tourism, health and education.
Knowledge-based activities: research and development, information technology and consulting.
The shift of an economy from mainly primary production towards manufacturing.
Public: owned by the state or a local authority. Private: owned by individuals or companies.
The stages from raw material to consumer; value is added at each stage by different firms.
The decline of manufacturing as a share of output and jobs, because of closure, relocation or higher productivity.
Rising incomes raise demand for services such as tourism, education and banking faster than for basic goods; technology also creates new services.
